claim: In experiment, compressed tetrahedral clusters of four 1.0-um polystyrene lobes whose retracted TPM patches carry self-complementary DNA crystallised into cubic diamond -- ABC stacking of the (111) honeycomb planes seen by confocal microscopy -- for compression ratios from 0.63 to 0.78 with size ratios near 1.2, the interlocked crystals reaching a particle volume fraction of about 0.68.

numbers.name: patch_protrusion_ratio
numbers.note: the size ratio the crystallising particles were near, stated as near 1.2.

numbers.name: packing_fraction
numbers.note: particle volume fraction in the interlocked crystals, stated as around 0.68.

validity_conditions: AN EXPERIMENT, NOT A MODEL RESULT. Compression ratio is the lobe centre-to-centre distance over the lobe diameter; size ratio is the patch's radial extent from the cluster centre over the lobe radius. Crystallised overnight in a 50/50 D2O/PBS buffer (10 mM, pH 7.4, 280 mM NaCl, 1 wt% F-127) in a capillary tilted about 20 degrees with a ~1 degC gradient spanning the DNA melting temperature of about 40 degC; crystals typically 40 um across, some beyond 100 um, about ten layers thick. The crystal volume fraction of about 0.68 compares with 0.74 for close packing and 0.34 for a diamond lattice of touching spheres.
